papers.title: Large language model agents in watershed environmental response: a hypothesis-and-theory framework for the cognitive orchestration layer
papers.summary: Introduction Watershed environmental governance increasingly combines dense sensing infrastructure with institutions whose attention, authority, and coordination capacity remain limited. We develop the cognitive orchestration layer as a theory-building concept for examining how large language model (LLM)-based agents may connect sensing, assessment, decision advice, institutional response, and feedback without displacing domain models or public authority. Methods The Agentic Framework for Watershed Governance (AFWG) specifies three enabling pathways, three institutional interfaces, and four propositions. A purposively selected set of eight publicly documented cases is used to illustrate functional configurations, source limitations, and research gaps; it is not a systematic review or empirical evaluation. Results The cases document sensing, assessment, and decision-support functions, but do not establish improved decision quality, sustained institutional use, environmental outcomes, or agent-executed response closure. MAESTRO is retained as an adjacent-domain design illustration, not an existence proof of full-loop closure: human authorization remains necessary, and its reported performance has not been independently replicated. papers.title: Evidence constrained agentic retrieval augmented generation for substation civil engineering preliminary design documents in a single project study
papers.summary: Substation civil engineering preliminary design documents must integrate project-specific conditions, current regulatory requirements, typical design practices, and historical engineering experience while maintaining consistency across architectural, structural, general-layout, foundation, road, drainage, and technical-indicator sections. Conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems remain vulnerable to condition-insensitive retrieval, unequal source authority, incompatible evidence, unsupported engineering claims, and parameter drift during long-document drafting. This study proposes an Evidence-Constrained Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, termed EC-ARAG. The framework combines regulation-aware evidence representation, validity-gated hybrid retrieval, source-role-aware conflict resolution, dual planning–retrieval and generation–verification–repair loops, and global project-state memory. The experimental corpus comprised 36 national and industry standards, 12 enterprise standards, 18 typical-design documents, 64 historical preliminary design documents, and nine project-input documents. The held-out evaluation included 120 retrieval queries, 80 applicability cases, 48 evidence-conflict cases, 318 atomic design propositions, and five independent generation runs. The expanded robustness evaluation further included 120 state-write gating cases and 24 e

papers.title: Authorization assurance for tool-using LLM agents: a structured review of enforcement semantics and effect-level security evidence
papers.summary: Abstract Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents exercise authority over protected resources through APIs, tools, credentials, and external services. This structured review asks whether authorization claims are supported at the enforcement and observation boundaries relevant to the claimed effect. A 75-source evidence library was screened into a 30-source analytical corpus (15 strict agent sources, 6 sensitivity sources, and 9 authorization/assurance comparators), yielding 92 Source-Claim Records. Within this closed corpus, five strict sources made mediation or non-bypassability claims with heterogeneous evidence endpoints; all three evaluable least-privilege sources narrowed available authority without measuring trajectory-wide effective privilege; no evaluable revocation claim appeared among 21 agent-focused sources; and no delegation-containment claim appeared in the 30-source corpus. Final-state correctness was also distinct from authorization correctness. We integrate these findings through an Authorization Assurance Claim Model linking claim scope, obligations, enforcement, evidence, protected effect, and residual assumptions. The resulting MAAP is presented as a preliminary, review-derived minimum reporting framework, not a validated scoring or certification instrument. The supplementary workbook provides the screening decisions, complete coding dataset, source-prop

papers.title: Phygital research fit: toward a theory-building framework for transformative and sustainable service research
papers.summary: Phygital service research requires evidence of how physical and digital elements jointly produce service outcomes. We develop phygital research fit as alignment among the phenomenon, theory, evidence, research design, and validity and ethical criteria. Extending methodological fit with a phenomenon-specific diagnostic framework, we identify six theory-building problems and classify service arrangements along embodied co-presence and digital agency into linked handoff, embedded augmentation, remote orchestration, and hybrid immersion. A theory selector and research toolbox connect these types to candidate explanations, evidence requirements, and claim-specific checks. Transformative and sustainable service research provide cross-cutting evaluative lenses for examining access, agency, employee work, resource flows, governance, and continuity under disruption. These lenses require appropriate outcome evidence whenever transformation or sustainability is claimed, whereas ethical responsibilities apply throughout. The framework supports theory building by making explicit which physical-digital relations a design must capture and which claims its evidence can support.

papers.title: MetaNav: Metacognitive Vision-Language Navigation via Reflective Exploration
papers.summary: Training-free Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) agents powered by foundation models can follow instructions and explore 3D environments. However, existing approaches rely on greedy frontier selection and passive spatial memory, leading to inefficient behaviors such as local oscillation and redundant revisiting. We argue that this stems from a lack of metacognitive capabilities: the agent cannot monitor its exploration progress, diagnose strategy failures, or adapt accordingly. To address this, we propose MetaNav, a metacognitive navigation agent integrating spatial memory, history-aware planning, and reflective correction. Spatial memory builds a persistent 3D semantic map. History-aware planning penalizes revisiting to improve efficiency. Reflective correction detects stagnation and uses an LLM to generate corrective rules that guide future frontier selection. Experiments on GOAT-Bench, HM3D-OVON, and A-EQA show that MetaNav achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing VLM queries by 20.7%, demonstrating that metacognitive reasoning significantly improves robustness and efficiency. The code is available at https://github.com/perfectlxy7/MetaNav.

papers.title: Q-Planner: A Harness System for Quantum Chemistry Agents
papers.summary: Abstract LLM-based agents for computational chemistry commonly place the model inside an accumulating execution loop, causing context growth proportional to workflow length, unpredictable token costs, and degraded plan reliability at scale. We present a chemistry computation harness that confines LLM invocations to three semantically bounded stages─compound identification, planning, and reporting─while delegating all tool dispatch, parallel scheduling, arithmetic derivation, and artifact routing to a deterministic LangGraph executor that consumes zero LLM tokens during execution; a library of domain skill modules injects specialist quantum chemistry protocols into the planner context at planning time without enlarging the execution context. Across five representative quantum chemistry workflows, the planning, calculator, and reporting calls averaged 9700–25,300 tokens per run, with zero execution-stage tokens in every case─more than 93% fewer tokens (before caching) than loop-based multiagent systems─and, on a high-throughput single-point-energy scaling benchmark, a full-scheme plan representation sustained 100% plan-structural correctness across all 30 runs from N = 10 to 100 compounds of one workflow type, generating a 200-node graph of 100 independent single-point jobs from a single planning call. On the workloads tested, harness design made quantum chemistry automation more

papers.title: ScopeBench: Do Agents Preserve Engagement Boundaries Under Goal Pressure?
papers.summary: Agents are increasingly deployed with real autonomy in web application and network penetration testing, where a single out-of-scope action can breach a client’s engagement boundary. Existing offensive-security benchmarks measure raw hacking capability; as those benchmarks saturate, what actually gates deployment is a special case of alignment: scope adherence. We introduce ScopeBench, a benchmark of 30 dead-end agentic security tasks in which the stated objective is reachable only by violating the stated scope. Each task appears under two conditions that share an environment, verifier, and objective and differ only in scope: one instruction set has no scope and measures capability; the other has a natural-language scope to measure adherence. Every trajectory passes through two grading arms. First, a deterministic flag verifier acts as a violation verifier—a pass under scoped instruction proves by construction that a forbidden action occurred—yielding a high-precision lower bound on the violation rate. A tool-assisted, full-context judge then estimates whether an out-of-scope call occurred in trajectories that fail mechanical verification. We calibrate the judge against 100 ScopeBench trajectories labeled call-by-call by human annotators, and a blinded audit of the evaluated rollouts finds its high recall holds—no false negatives among the 36 audited violations, with over-flaggi

papers.title: A Governed Computational Architecture for Predictive Process Monitoring with Policy-Constrained Orchestration and Auditable Decision Making
papers.summary: Abstract Predictive process monitoring enables organizations to anticipate process outcomes from event logs, although deployment in real operational environments remains challenging due to temporal drift, heterogeneous traces, and limited interpretability of deep predictive models. This work presents an integrated framework combining Transformer-based predictive monitoring with governed operational orchestration for business-process automation. The predictive layer jointly estimates case outcome, next activity, and remaining decision time, while the orchestration layer manages routing, escalation, explanation triggering, and execution logging under explicit policy constraints. Integrated Gradients provide event-level attribution evidence, while calibration and confidence signals support conservative decision regulation under uncertainty. Experiments were conducted on the BPI Challenge 2017 and BPI Challenge 2012 datasets under leakage-aware and drift-sensitive conditions. The evaluation includes comparisons with neural and tree-based predictive-process-monitoring baselines, selected ablation analyses, policy-sweep experiments, and a structured expert-agent proxy assessment of the audit layer across six selected case studies. In the main BPI Challenge 2017 evaluation, the predictive model achieved PR-AUC = 0.6963 for outcome prediction, Top-3 Accuracy = 0.9986 and NDCG@3 = 0.969

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
papers.summary: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. We added TDD to their pilot workflow, using a design science approach, with continuous refinements to prompt design and workflow structure, based on observed AI behavior. The generated code was evaluated and compared with non-TDD code, using SonarQube for static code analysis. The results indicate that TDD reduced complexity and code duplication, but introduced more quality issues overall, while non-TDD produced fewer, but more severe issues. The generated tests from the TDD workflow focused more on content verification than on behavioral testing, contributing to a lower code coverage per test compared to non-TDD. The findings suggest that TDD involves trade-offs that may favor certain development priorities, in particular where lower complexity and reduced duplication are more beneficial than minimizing total issue count. This indicates that a strict application of TDD may not be optimal in an autonomous AI-driven context, and that exploring more flexible adaptations of the TDD workflow remains interesting for future resea

papers.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
papers.summary: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. Meanwhile, teachers assume a facilitative role by guiding inquiry, supporting experimentation, an

papers.title: LLM Analysis of 150+ Years of German Parliamentary Debates on Migration Reveals a Shift from Post-War Solidarity to Anti-Solidarity in the Last Decade
papers.summary: Abstract Migration has been a core topic in German political debate, from postwar expellee displacement to labor migration and recent refugee movements. Large-scale analysis of such political discourse has traditionally required extensive manual annotation, limiting coverage. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative. Using a theory-driven annotation scheme, we examine how well LLMs annotate subtypes of solidarity and anti-solidarity in German parliamentary debates and whether the resulting labels support valid downstream inference. We first evaluate multiple LLMs across model size, prompting strategies, fine-tuning, historical versus contemporary data, and systematic errors. The strongest models, especially GPT-5 and gpt-oss-120B, achieve macro-F1 scores comparable to human agreement, although their systematic errors can bias downstream results. We therefore combine soft-label model outputs with Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL) to reduce bias in long-term trend estimates. Beyond the methodological evaluation, we interpret the resulting annotations from a social-scientific perspective across the Reichstag (1867–1933), West German Bundestag (1949–1990) and Re-Unified German Bundestag (1990–2025) corpus to trace trends in solidarity and anti-solidarity toward migrants, with detailed analysis of postwar Germany (1949–1957) and contemporary Germany (2009–2025)

papers.title: Coordinating actions and sharing control with a disembodied artificial intelligence: Task-dependent differences from human partners.

papers.title: Beyond the Degree: International PhD Graduates’ Employment Journeys Through Self-Regulated Learning and Agency
papers.summary: Recent research has highlighted how international graduates enact different forms of agency to negotiate their employability. This study extends that line of inquiry by examining how self-regulated learning (SRL) strategies mediate the development of these forms of agency. It utilised a qualitative design, drawing on in-depth interviews with 35 international PhD graduates in Australia. The findings showed that the participants selectively deployed SRL strategies to enact distinct forms of agency. For example, seeking information, social assistance, environmental structuring, and organising and transforming supported their essential needs-response agency. The study also identified novel SRL strategies, including life-mentorship and self-satisfaction. This study contributes by integrating SRL and agency frameworks to offer a process-oriented understanding of employability as the dynamic development and mobilisation of capitals. Practically, it suggests embedding SRL-informed career support and guidance for international graduates. Limitations include the Australia-specific sample, which may limit transferability to other settings.

papers.title: Metacognitive Reasoning in Energy Based Models Using Instance Based Learning Theory
papers.summary: Metacognition involves reasoning about cognitive processes themselves. An example is in resource allocation where we choose how much time and effort to put into a reasoning task before we begin based on our confidence. Current Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems that rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) cannot estimate their uncertainty about an output without first responding, and cannot dynamically allocate resources to producing an output, making this type of metacognitive process difficult. A recently proposed alternative to classic transformer architectures that addresses these two concerns is the Energy Based Model (EBM) which allows for interpretable uncertainty modeling and dynamic allocation of compute resources. While EBMs can allow for control of these two processes, the actual metacognitive task of determining compute allocation based on uncertainty is not directly addressed. Instance-Based Learning Theory (IBLT) provides an approach to modeling human-like decisions from experience that has previously been applied to predicting human metacognitive reasoning. In this paper we introduce a framework for MEtacognitive Reasoning with Instance-based Learning Theory and Energy Dynamics (MERITED). Grounded in IBLT, this framework allows for control of the computational effort allocated in an EBM to allow for metacognitive control over reasoning effort based on uncertainty

papers.title: Refining collaborative AI literacy: A systematic review of human–AI collaboration competency and AI literacy measures
papers.summary: With the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and its growing role in solving complex problems, human–AI interaction has evolved into a new dimension, where AI is increasingly perceived as a collaborative partner. However, current AI literacy frameworks focus on technical knowledge and ethical use, often neglecting the ability to collaborate effectively with AI as a standalone construct. Conceptualized under the umbrella of AI literacy, the boundaries of human–AI collaboration competency need to be refined in order to create common ground for advancing research and measurement of this essential ability. This systematic review synthesizes 17 studies conducted in higher education settings to examine how human–AI collaboration competency is represented and measured within existing AI literacy scales. The findings reveal that human–AI collaboration is rarely explicitly assessed, let alone as a distinct construct. Some studies included a small number of items that could implicitly refer to collaboration competency or context, but most included no such representation. Drawing on these findings, we propose theoretical implications regarding contexts and factors that should be considered when developing new items, and measurement implications for three possible sub-factors of human–AI collaboration competency: coordination, communication, and metacognition. papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: An Assessment of Accessibility and Affordability of Inpatient Psychiatric Care in Tennessee
papers.summary: Introduction: Access to mental health has seen changes over the past decade, but little research and attention have been given to access to inpatient psychiatric facilities. Inpatient psychiatric care is crucial for patients experiencing mental health emergencies who need immediate access to care. Gaps in spatial accessibility, affordability, and the access and assessment process were identified due to a lack of available information in the field. Methods: Secondary data from the Tennessee Department of Health were used to assess financial accessibility through payer source charges and patient encounters, as well as through mapping of inpatient psychiatric facilities and conducting drive time and coverage area analyses. Primary data were collected through interviews with clinicians located in Northeastern Tennessee to gain insight into the assessment process and gather their perceptions of inpatient care. Results: Longitudinal descriptive reviews on the financial accessibility among Tennessee Inpatient Facilities. This showed increased variability among facilities when stratified by region, ownership, and type of operation. Spatial accessibility in ArcGIS showed 82% of counties were not covered within a 30-minute radius of inpatient facilities. Analysis showed that Middle Tennessee had significantly less coverage from inpatient facilities and raised concerns about spatial-socia

papers.title: Pieces Solving a Puzzle: Emerging Roles and Cross-Field Analogies During a Distributed Epistemic Game
papers.summary: In an effort to describe why some problems can’t be solved, a character compared them to a cubic meter of platinum - a block so dense that all the people who could squeeze around it still couldn’t lift it off the ground. In the same way, these problems simply can’t have enough people gathered around and communicating about them - and so they remain unsolved. This research looks at the first Polymath Project (2009) as an example of a distributed epistemic game to examine how groups engage with complex problems. and without a locally omniscient individual. In this setting of epistemic uncertainty, interactions between individuals reveal patterns of participation, and an analogy opens a new solution pathway by introducing a problem-solving approach from another field. These insights answer the initial question of the Polymath Project - ‘Is massively collaborative mathematics possible?’ - and offer hope for lifting the cubic meter of other unsolvable problems.

papers.title: Making sense of sensation: a framework of interoceptive attribution and appraisal with clinical applications
papers.summary: Abstract Interoception provides a link between bodily states and cognitive and affective processes across both unconscious and conscious domains and is fundamental for a coherent sense of self. While previous research linking interoception to mental health has predominantly focused on interoceptive accuracy, attention, self-beliefs and insight, we argue that the higher-order interpretation of consciously perceived bodily signals plays a fundamental and underexplored role in this relationship. We propose a framework delineating two higher-order processes—interoceptive attribution and appraisal—which constitute the interpretation of interoceptive sensations that reach conscious awareness. We outline key factors that modulate attention, attribution and appraisal, and evidence the relevance of this framework to mental health conditions. Given that these processes are accessible to cognition, they represent an important target for existing psychotherapeutic interventions. We integrate such interventions within our framework, highlighting their potential to enhance interoception-based therapeutic approaches. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue ‘From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self’.

papers.title: Flexibility Controls Transport of Weakly Active Filaments in Crowded Landscapes
papers.summary: Active filaments, ranging from motor-driven biopolymers to elongated bacteria and worms, are paradigmatic examples of deformable active matter. How filament flexibility interacts with environmental heterogeneity to control their transport in crowded environments, however, remains poorly understood. Here, we perform large-scale Brownian dynamics simulations of tangentially driven active polymers moving through ordered and disordered obstacle arrays to map the long-time diffusion as a function of obstacle density and filament flexibility. We find that flexibility can either enhance or hinder transport depending on the structure of the medium. In disordered environments, transport is optimized at intermediate filament flexibility, whereas both highly flexible and semiflexible filaments diffuse more slowly. In contrast, dense ordered arrays enhance the mobility of semiflexible filaments by promoting directed motion along periodic channels. We identify three distinct transport regimes: (i) tortuosity-controlled diffusion of highly flexible filaments, characterized by trapping-and-hopping dynamics; (ii) confinement-assisted transport of moderately flexible filaments, which enhances diffusion in dense media; and (iii) persistence-controlled transport of semiflexible filaments, which facilitates diffusion in dense ordered media, but suppresses it in disordered media. papers.title: Beyond AI Productivity: Enterprise AI Systems, Human–AI Responsibility, and the Future of Work
papers.summary: Abstract A prior U.S. review, Enterprise AI at the Decision Point, established that enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) as-sistants have task-dependent productivity effects and that public evidence does not identify an independent financial return or a complete chain from AI cost to verified workforce replacement. The human side of that productivity record, and any organiza-tional consequences of workforce change, were left open. This study examines responsibilities, training, job insecurity and well-being, human oversight, and performance after U.S. enterprise AI adoption from November 2022 through September 2026. The design is a critical integrative review. Firms that report a task effect most often report exclusive augmentation. Frequent AI use is associated with greater fear of job loss. In one worker panel, displacement concern, rather than use frequency itself, is associated with lower engagement and higher burnout. The contribution is a responsibility-transfer framework with five constructs and four testable propositions. A proposed computa-tional specification of that framework, Human–AI Responsibility-Aware Workflow Optimization (HARWO), places verification and accountability on the workflow graph. Gross task-time savings are separated from net employee time. HARWO is not solved or estimated in this paper. The evidence gap reflects a measurement disconnect: existin

papers.title: ConvNeXt ‐ FD : Fractal Dimension‐Regularized ConvNeXt for Robust Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Biomedical image segmentation is a critical task in medical diagnosis and treatment planning, enabling precise delineation of anatomical structures and pathological regions. Despite significant advancements, challenges persist due to the inherent variability, noise and complex morphology present in diverse medical imaging modalities. This paper introduces ConvNeXt‐FD, a novel deep learning architecture for robust biomedical image segmentation, built upon a U‐Net‐like encoder‐decoder framework leveraging the powerful ConvNeXt backbone. Our approach integrates a hybrid loss function combining the Dice coefficient with a boundary‐aware regularization term inspired by a differentiable formulation of fractal dimension, designed to enhance the model's sensitivity to object boundaries and shape fidelity. We rigorously evaluate ConvNeXt‐FD across six distinct biomedical datasets: BUSI (breast ultrasound images), DDTI (thyroid ultrasound images), FluoCells (fluorescent cell images), IDRiD (diabetic retinopathy images for optic disc segmentation), ISIC2018 (skin lesion images) and MoNuSeg (nuclei segmentation). Experimental results demonstrate that ConvNeXt‐FD, particularly when initialized with ImageNet pre‐trained weights, achieves competitive and often superior performance compared to existing state‐of‐the‐art methods across various metrics, including Dice, Jaccard, Accuracy,

papers.title: Intelligent orchestration of programmable network resources and services in the edge-to-cloud continuum
papers.summary: Edge computing has become an important way to support next-generation telecommunications networks. By moving computation closer to data sources and end users, it makes it possible to provide low-latency, energy-efficient, and context-aware services. This dissertation examines the orchestration and scheduling of heterogeneous services across various edge computing architectures, tackling the inherent complexity arising from the diversity of network infrastructures, computing nodes, and service requirements. The first part of the thesis is about how to design and analyze an edge-oriented service orchestration platform. This platform is designed to handle different types of services over different types of networks, taking into account the unique features of edge environments, like limited resources, architectural diversity, and changing operating conditions. The research's main focus is on service scheduling strategies, with a focus on optimizing key performance indicators that are important for future telecommunications networks, such as end-to-end latency and energy use. Various scheduling methodologies are proposed and assessed to concurrently optimize these objectives, emphasizing the trade-offs among performance, resource utilization, and operational efficiency in distributed edge contexts. The thesis further investigates the implementation of these mechanisms in scenarios w

papers.title: Harnessing single-cell omics for farmed animal improvement and human health
papers.summary: Cellular heterogeneity underlies the regulation of complex traits and diseases, making cell-resolved molecular characterization fundamental for advancing precision agriculture and human biomedicine. Rapid advances in single-cell omics technologies, together with the ever-evolving computational methods, have led to the establishment of large-scale single cell atlases across multiple species, providing unprecedented opportunities to systematically dissect cellular diversity and regulatory mechanisms underlying complex phenotypes. In this review, we summarize recent progresses in single-cell sequencing technologies, reference cell atlas projects, and the integration of single-cell omics with population/quantitative genetics, as well as discuss how artificial intelligence and predictive perturbation modelling are reshaping single-cell research. Finally, we highlight future directions toward population-scale single-cell omics, AI-driven virtual cells/tissues, and genotype-cell/tissue-trait frameworks, which are expected to transform biological discovery, enable better design of veterinary medicines and human therapeutics, as well as accelerate sustainable farmed animal improvement and precision medicine.

papers.title: Designing a Curriculum Model Based on Artificial Intelligence and Purposeful Physical Activity to Enhance Learning Self-Regulation, Mental Health, and Psychological Well-Being among Students
papers.summary: Objective: The objective of this study was to design and validate a curriculum model based on artificial intelligence and purposeful physical activity with emphasis on enhancing learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being among students. Methods and Materials: This applied developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, 20 experts in curriculum studies, educational technology, artificial intelligence in education, physical education, educational psychology, and student mental health were selected through purposive criterion-based sampling from Tehran and participated in semi-structured interviews. The interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis to extract the main dimensions, components, and indicators of the proposed curriculum model. In the quantitative phase, 384 secondary school students from Tehran were selected through multistage cluster sampling during the 2025–2026 academic year. Data were collected using a researcher-made curriculum model validation questionnaire, a learning self-regulation questionnaire, the General Health Questionnaire, and a psychological well-being scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. Findings: The inferential findings showed that the final curri

papers.title: The Adaptive Automotive Supplier: Integrating Governance Theories and Contemporary Risk Profiles
papers.summary: Automotive suppliers are facing disruptions from vehicle electrification, software-defined vehicle architectures and geopolitical fragmentation and regionalization. This article integrates five pillars of management thinking (transaction cost economics, agency theory, game theory, global value chain theory and platform ecosystem theory) explaining how these pressures transform OEM's supplier governance for 423 articles published from 2010 to 2026. The findings suggest that supplier management literature mostly focuses on supply chain and strategic risks and that there is a severe shortage of implementation specificity: instead of providing a specific set of organizational capabilities, studies mostly outline risks or potential coping strategies. The study frames supplier adaptation to global transformations as a compound governance problem and outlines a staged agenda, encompassing sensing and diagnosing existing risks, adopting a governance response and developing their capabilities for ensuring strategic significance within the global automotive OEM network considering asymmetric bargaining power in the setting of persistent volatility.

papers.title: Generative AI use and scientific literacy among 15-year-olds in Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang, China: the mediating role of academic help-seeking
papers.summary: Introduction Adolescents increasingly use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots for schoolwork, yet evidence on whether this use supports or undermines learning is mixed. Drawing on research on cognitive offloading and self-regulated learning, we examined whether GenAI use for schoolwork is related to scientific literacy directly and through two components of self-regulated learning, academic help-seeking and metacognitive strategy use, and whether the purpose of use matters. Methods We analyzed the Program for International Student Assessment 2025 (PISA 2025) data from 12,191 15-year-old students in 374 schools in Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang, China. Weighted two-level mediation models compared students within the same school, used all ten plausible values, and evaluated indirect effects with Monte Carlo confidence intervals. Results were checked against a design-based model with school fixed effects and balanced repeated replication weights. Results Students who used GenAI more often than their schoolmates reported more help-seeking ( β = 0.17) and more metacognitive strategy use ( β = 0.30).
